translations.literal: Zhuo did not understand his meaning and supposed Weihan was speaking of Kong Ying; he therefore examined Ying and passed him. Public discussion greatly regarded this as wrong. [Zhuo] was immediately removed from the Hanlin Academy, appointed Left Assistant Director in the Ministry of State Affairs, and transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo misunderstood and thought Weihan meant to warn him against Kong Ying. He passed Ying in the examination instead, to widespread outrage. Zhuo was removed from the Hanlin Academy, made left assistant director in the Ministry of State Affairs, and transferred to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 五年，高祖詔太常復文武二舞，詳定正、冬朝會禮及樂章。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances, and to fix in detail the rites of the regular and winter court assemblies and their musical pieces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix the rites of the regular and winter court assemblies and their musical pieces.

sentences.zh: 自唐末之亂，禮樂制度亡失已久，棁與御史中丞竇貞固、刑部侍郎呂琦、禮部侍郎張允等草定之。

translations.literal: Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost; Zhuo, together with Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others, drafted and fixed them.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and music had been lost since the chaos at the end of Tang. Zhuo worked with Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister Lü Qi, Vice Minister Zhang Yun, and others to draft the regulations.

sentences.zh: 其年冬至，高祖會朝崇元殿，廷設宮縣，二舞在北，登歌在上。

translations.literal: That year at the winter solstice, Gaozu held court at the Chongyuan Hall; in the courtyard the palace musical sets were arranged, the two dances to the north, and the ascending song above.
translations.idiomatic: That winter solstice Gaozu held court in the Chongyuan Hall. Palace musical sets were arranged in the courtyard, with the two dances to the north and the ascending song above.

sentences.zh: 文舞郎八佾，六十有四人，冠進賢，黃紗袍，白中單，白練衤蓋襠，白布大口袴，革帶履。

translations.literal: The civil dance performers were eight rows, sixty-four in all, wearing advancing-worth caps, yellow gauze robes, white under-garments, white silk cover-bibs, white cloth broad trousers, leather belts and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: The civil dancers numbered eight rows, sixty-four in all, wearing advancing-worth caps, yellow gauze robes, white undergarments, white silk cover-bibs, white broad trousers, leather belts, and shoes.

sentences.zh: 左執籥，右秉翟。

translations.literal: In the left hand they held flutes; in the right, pheasant-feather staffs.
translations.idiomatic: They held flutes in the left hand and pheasant-feather staffs in the right.

sentences.zh: 執籥引者二人。

translations.literal: Two led holding flutes.
translations.idiomatic: Two leaders held flutes to lead them.

sentences.zh: 武舞郎八佾，六十有四人，服平巾幘，緋絲布大袖、繡襠甲金飾，白練衤蓋，錦騰蛇起梁帶，豹文大口袴，烏靴。

translations.literal: The military dance performers were eight rows, sixty-four in all, wearing plain headcloths, crimson silk broad sleeves, embroidered breastplates with gold ornament, white silk cover-bibs, brocade belts with rising beams and coiled serpents, leopard-pattern broad trousers, and black boots.
translations.idiomatic: The military dancers numbered eight rows, sixty-four in all, wearing plain headcloths, crimson broad sleeves, gold-trimmed embroidered breastplates, white silk cover-bibs, brocade belts with serpent patterns, leopard-pattern trousers, and black boots.

sentences.zh: 左執幹，右執戚。

translations.literal: In the left hand they held shields; in the right, axes.
translations.idiomatic: They held shields in the left hand and axes in the right.

sentences.zh: 執旌引者二人。

translations.literal: Two led holding banners.
translations.idiomatic: Two leaders held banners to lead them.

sentences.zh: 加鼓吹十二按，負以熊釣，以象百獸率舞。

translations.literal: Added were twelve sets of wind and percussion, bearing bear-hooks on the back, to represent the hundred beasts leading the dance.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve sets of wind and percussion were added, with bear-hooks on the performers' backs to represent the hundred beasts leading the dance.

sentences.zh: 按設羽葆鼓一，大鼓一，金錞一。

translations.literal: Each set had one feather-canopied drum, one large drum, and one metal chime.
translations.idiomatic: Each set included one feather-canopied drum, one large drum, and one metal chime.

sentences.zh: 歌、簫、笳各二人。

translations.literal: Singers, vertical flutes, and horns, two of each.
translations.idiomatic: There were two singers, two vertical flutists, and two horn players.

sentences.zh: 王公上壽，天子舉爵，奏《玄同》；

translations.literal: When dukes and princes offered longevity wishes, the Son of Heaven raised his cup and they performed Dark Unity;
translations.idiomatic: When nobles offered longevity wishes, the emperor raised his cup and they performed Dark Unity.

sentences.zh: 三舉，登歌奏《文同》；

translations.literal: at the third raising, the ascending song performed Literary Unity;
translations.idiomatic: At the third raising, the ascending song performed Literary Unity.

sentences.zh: 舉食，文舞舞《昭德》，武舞舞《成功》之曲。

translations.literal: when food was raised, the civil dance danced to Manifest Virtue and the military dance danced to the tune of Accomplished Success.
translations.idiomatic: When food was served, the civil dancers performed Manifest Virtue and the military dancers performed Accomplished Success.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，高祖大悅，賜棁金帛，群臣左右睹者皆嗟嘆之。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk on Zhuo; the hundred officials and those around who witnessed it all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites ended, Gaozu was delighted and rewarded Zhuo with gold and silk. Every official who witnessed it sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 然禮樂廢久，而制作簡繆，又繼以龜茲部《霓裳法曲》，參亂雅音，其樂工舞郎，多教坊伶人、百工商賈、州縣避役之人，又無老師良工教習。

translations.literal: Yet ritual and music had long been abandoned, and the production was crude and erroneous; moreover the Kucha department's Rainbow Skirt Dharma Tune was mixed in, disturbing refined music. Most of the musicians and dance performers were entertainers from the Instruction Quarter, artisans and merchants, and men from prefectures and counties avoiding corvée labor—and there were no veteran masters or skilled craftsmen to teach them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ritual and music had long lain in ruins, and the production was crude and flawed. The Kucha Rainbow Skirt tune was mixed in, corrupting refined music. Most musicians and dancers were Instruction Quarter entertainers, artisans, merchants, and men dodging corvée from the provinces, with no veteran masters to train them.

sentences.zh: 明年正旦，復奏於廷，而登歌發聲悲離煩慝，如《薤露》、《虞殯》之音，舞者行列進退，皆不應節，聞者皆悲憤。

translations.literal: The next year on New Year's Day they performed again at court, but the ascending song's voices were mournful, discordant, and vexed, like the tones of Thoroughwort Dew and Yu's Funeral; the dancers' ranks advancing and retreating all failed to match the beat, and those who heard were all grieved and indignant.
translations.idiomatic: The next New Year's Day they performed again at court, but the ascending song sounded mournful and discordant, like funeral dirges. The dancers' ranks advanced and retreated out of time, and all who heard were grieved and indignant.

sentences.zh: 其年高祖崩。

translations.literal: That year Gaozu died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Gaozu died.

sentences.zh: 棁以風痹改太子賓客分司西京以卒。

translations.literal: Zhuo, on account of wind paralysis, was changed to Guest of the Heir Apparent with a separate commission in the western capital, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was reassigned on account of rheumatism to guest of the heir apparent with a separate commission in the western capital, where he died.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，太常少卿陶穀奏廢二舞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun, the Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Tao Gu memorialized to abolish the two dances.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyun, Vice Director Tao Gu of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized to abolish the two dances.

sentences.zh: 明年，契丹滅晉，耶律德光入京師，太常請備法駕奉迎，樂工教習鹵簿鼓吹，都人聞者為之流涕焉。

translations.literal: The next year the Khitan destroyed Jin; Yelü Deguang entered the capital. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices requested preparing the imperial carriage to welcome him; musicians rehearsed the guard-of-honor wind and percussion. People of the capital who heard it wept for it.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Khitans destroyed Later Jin and Yelü Deguang entered the capital. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices prepared the imperial carriage to welcome him, and musicians rehearsed the guard-of-honor music. People of the capital wept when they heard it.

sentences.zh: ○李懌

translations.literal: Li Yi
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi

sentences.zh: 李懌，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Li Yi was a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi was from Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少好學，頗工文辭。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and was quite skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning from youth and wrote with considerable skill.

sentences.zh: 唐末舉進士，為秘書省校書郎、集賢校理。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang he passed the jinshi examination and became Proofreader in the Palace Library and Collator in the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tang he passed the jinshi examination and became proofreader in the Palace Library and collator in the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.

sentences.zh: 唐亡，事梁為監察御史，累遷中書舍人、翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Tang perished he served Liang as Attending Censor and rose in succession to Secretariat Drafter and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang fell he served Later Liang as attending censor and rose to secretariat drafter and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 梁亡，責授懷州司馬，遇赦量移，稍遷衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: When Liang perished he was punished by appointment as military adjutant of Huaizhou; encountering an amnesty he was transferred by degree and gradually promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Liang fell he was demoted to military adjutant of Huaizhou. After an amnesty he was gradually restored and promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 天成中，復為中書舍人、翰林學士，累遷尚書右丞承旨。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era he was again made Secretariat Drafter and Hanlin Academician, and rose in succession to Right Assistant Director in the Ministry of State Affairs and Chief Academician.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng era he was restored as secretariat drafter and Hanlin academician and rose to right assistant director in the Ministry of State Affairs and chief academician.

sentences.zh: 時右散騎常侍張文寶知貢舉，所放進士，中書有覆落者，乃請下學士院作詩賦為貢舉格，學士竇夢徵、張礪等所作不工，乃命懌為之，懌笑曰：「年少舉進士登科，蓋偶然爾。

translations.literal: At that time the Right Regular Attendant Zhang Wenbao was in charge of the examination; among the jinshi he passed, some were struck down on review by the Secretariat. He thereupon requested that the Hanlin Academy produce poetry and rhapsodies as examination standards. The compositions of Academicians Dou Mengzheng, Zhang Li, and others were unskilled, so Yi was ordered to do it. Yi laughed and said, "Passing the jinshi examination and entering the roster in youth was merely accidental."
translations.idiomatic: Right regular attendant Zhang Wenbao was then in charge of the examination. Some of his passed candidates were struck down on Secretariat review, so he asked the Hanlin Academy to compose model poetry and rhapsodies for the examination. The efforts of Dou Mengzheng, Zhang Li, and others were inadequate, and Yi was ordered to write them. Yi laughed and said that passing the jinshi in youth had been mere accident.

sentences.zh: 後生可畏，來者未可量，假令予復就禮部試，未必不落第，安能與英俊為準格？

translations.literal: The young are to be feared; those who come after cannot yet be measured. Supposing I were to take the Ministry of Rites examination again, I might not necessarily fail—but how could I set the standard together with the talented?
translations.idiomatic: The young are formidable and the future cannot be measured. If I took the Ministry of Rites examination again, I might well fail. How could I set the standard for talented men?

sentences.zh: 」聞者多其知體。

translations.literal: Those who heard mostly praised his understanding of propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard praised his sense of propriety.

sentences.zh: 後遷刑部尚書分司洛陽，卒，年七十餘。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Minister of Justice with a separate commission in Luoyang; he died, aged more than seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made minister of justice with a separate commission in Luoyang and died in his seventies.
